description: Waterfront Restaurant Rebuilds to Remain Open Through Future Storms is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by FEMA, Federal Emergency Management Agency; Jacques Cousteau National Estuarine Research Reserve; NOAA Office for Coastal Management. Property owners in New Jersey can check their vulnerability to sea level rise and storm surge using an interactive mapping tool, the NJ Flood Mapper. Here's how one restaurant owner used results from the tool in his long-term planning. Coverage: New Jersey (2014). The toolkit gives New Jersey as the location, 2014 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
